notes.title: I'm sorry for being gone for so long.
notes.content:
Hello to everyone that has shown interest, or even just curiosity, in "Broken Dungeon."

As many of you may have noticed, there has been little to no word from me in regards to the development of the game, and I am sincerely apologetic about that.

I'd like to take this moment to not only reassure you that the game is not dead in the water, but to share where I have been.

To bring anyone new to this game up to speed, the last update/correspondence from me was back in October of last year.  As a game in "Early Access" and from a brand new developer in the industry, this likely caused many to feel the game has become a dead project.  That interpretation is understandable.

To anyone that has supported the game's development and been excited for its future, this may have felt like a let down, or even a slap to the face.

Again, I wish to express my apologies for dropping off the face of the planet.

For almost a year,  I have had to set the development of Broken Dungeon on the back burner.

The cause was due to instability in my life and living situations.  Without a stable home, I simply could not think about game development or anything even extra-curricular.

I regret that I did not release a statement about this earlier, but I was simply laser focused on re-establishing my life and home.  For quite some time, it was 24/7 "crunch time" on just finding a place to live.

I do have good news, though.  I have obtained a new home, and secured a wonderful job in the development industry.  With that said, I can now comfortably return to working on "Broken Dungeon" more regularly.

I am looking forward to continuing to advance "Broken Dungeon" into the game I had envisioned, and even more-so into the game the community desires.

With that said, I plan to dedicate my upcoming development of BD to addressing a few bugs that were brought to my attention (i.e. the Battleaxe disappearing when thrown) and the significant improvement to the Dungeon Master role.  This will include adding new capabilities to the Dungeon Master, and working to make the role feel more rewarding to play (rather than acting as a troll or a chore to the VR player).  Furthermore, these new capabilities that I have planned will reveal themselves as new interactions for the VR player, as well.

(I'm sure many of you have felt that the game loop of simply find alters, open alters, open door, beat the boss, and repeat has gotten old pretty fast.)

So, please look forward to the continuation of Broken Dungeon's development, and I appreciate all of you for being patient and sticking with me.

- Ken (SLAMS Games)

TLDR: Life got flipped upside down, but now I've learned to walk on the ceiling.  New home, new job, and I can return to dedicating time to Broken Dungeon's future.

notes.title: Broken Dungeon v0.5.2.5 set as default version
notes.content:
With no reports of major bugs, the default version of Broken Dungeon has been updated to v0.5.2.5.

As a reminder, here is the change log for this version:

====================================

Change Log:
(v0.5.2.5)
Additions:
- The hammer melee weapon gets some love with its new "Impact Spike" utility function.  Once charged, the hammer will spawn an ethereal spike.  Hitting the spike with the hammer will split the spike into 5 and send them flying outward as a ranged piercing attack.  Challenging to aim correctly, but effective against groups of monsters.

Changes:
- (QoL Fix) Hammer collider shape changed to be more forgiving on players that are closer to their target than they thought.

- (Bug Fix) Modified monster nav-pathing to re-initialize its pathfinding logic if its end destination doesn't correctly relate to the VR player's position. Thus, fixing the issue of monsters pathing into walls instead of to the player.

- (Bug Fix) Corrected logic error in magic that caused "The Devil On Your Shoulder" to deal zero damage.

- (Bug Fix) Modified logic on "Chain Lightning" and "Frigid Lance" spells that caused a memory leak.

Other:
- N/A

notes.title: Going Forward
notes.content:
Greetings, adventurers.

I know it has been longer than usual for the next update to Broken Dungeon.  I apologize for the wait.  Some life events occurred which pulled me away from being able to dedicate as much time to Broken Dungeon as I wanted to.

Fear not, though, as development is still active and thriving.  The next update will continue the addition of the melee weapon utility functions, and some quality of life and bug fixes.  Once all of the melee weapon utility functions are implemented, I will be dedicating myself to refining and improving the Dungeon Master role.  Things on the list are:
- Traps for purchase and placement
- Monster Stats upgrades for purchase
- New DM abilities
- Refining DM player engagement and actions to be more fun
- Quality of Life updates

As always, I want to hear from the community on what you like, don't like, want to see, don't want to see, etc.  This game is as much as yours as it is mine, so I want it to be something we are all proud of and enjoy playing.

Thank you all for your patience, and I look forward to continuing to improve the Broken Dungeon experience.

-Ken (SLAMS Games)

notes.title: v0.5.2.4 upgraded to default version.
notes.content:
Greetings, adventurers.

With no reports of major bugs, Broken Dungeon v0.5.2.4 has been upgraded out of beta into the new default version of the game.

As a reminder, here is the change log for the version:

=======================================================

Change log:
(v0.5.2.4)
Additions:
- Armor clad monsters beware!  The Spear's utility function "Pierce" is now available.  While charged, "Pierce" will auto-trigger when the adventurer strikes a monster or breakable object with a straight-forward thrust.  (Slashing will not trigger "Pierce")

- Due to some adventurers dropping spells right at their own feet, tip card 17 has been added to the title scene to explain about throwable spells and weapon utilities.

- The adventurer's guild has updated their Tips & Tricks guide book.  Tip card 14 now displays a video demonstrating some of the weapon utility functions in action.

Changes:
- (Bug Fix) Modified monster attack logic to ensure their attack delay gets reset when they are stunned.

- (Bug Fix) Modified weapon swapping logic to stop player from being able to swap their weapon if it is in the middle of a thrown utility effect.  Player must wait for the weapon to return before it can be swapped for a new weapon.

- (Bug Fix) Modified hand-held map logic to stop player from being able to pull out their map if their weapon is in a thrown utility effect.  Player must wait for the weapon to return before it can be swapped for the map.

- (QoL Fix) Tip card 14's text has been updated to better explain weapon utilities.

- (QoL Fix) Tip card 14's disclaimer has been updated from "Not Implemented Yet" to "Work In Progress" to reflect the partial development of the weapon utilities.

- (QoL Fix) Tip card 15's disclaimer has been updated to more properly inform players that only the "Shock" debuff has not been implemented yet.

- (QoL Fix) Game Options now has an option to allow Index Knuckle users to choose if they want squeezing the grip or touching the thumbpad to be the input for magic/weapon swapping, door opening, and general object interactions.

- (QoL Fix) When human input via the mouse is detected to disable the AI Dungeon Master, the VR View window will now shrink to the bottom right of the screen (if it was full screen).  Then, if the AI Dungeon Master is re-enabled, the VR View window will resume being full screen if the option "VR View Fullscreen" is enabled in the title scene options.

- (Visual Fix) Firestorm spell now fades out of existence instead of simply popping out of existence.

- (Bug Fix) Weapons now properly refresh their attack cool down upon recovering thrown weapons and weapon swapping.

- (Bug Fix) Alter warping logic has been corrected to ensure VR player properly warps to the alters sequentially and avoid warping back to the same alter.

- (Visual Fix) Fire Bolt spell's projectile now illuminates the dungeon slightly more brightly to better match its particle effect more closely.

Other:
- N/A

notes.title: v0.5.2.1 Now In Beta Status
notes.content:
Good evening, adventurers!

I have just uploaded a work-in-progress build of Broken Dungeon as version 0.5.2.1.  It can be accessed via the Beta selector menu within your Steam library.

This build of the game has the utility functions for the Gladius "Double Strike" and Bastard Sword "Pulse Wave" implemented.  To use the utility function, hold down the right hand trigger until the controller begins to vibrate.  Releasing the trigger will then activate the utility.  The utility function will only charge if your weapon's attack cool down has fully refreshed.

[u]Gladius "Double Strike"[/u] - Spawns an ethereal hand and sword that mimics the last 1-second of movement of your own right hand.

[u]Bastard Sword "Pulse Wave"[/u] - Blasts out a pressure wave from the tip of the sword that pushes monsters away from the epicenter.

As additional utility functions are developed for the other weapons, this work-in-progress beta will be updated.

If you encounter strange behavior or glitches, please let me know.

As always, keep on adventuring!!!
-Ken (SLAMS Games)

- The general level of the local adventurers has risen, giving birth to a new instinct.  The right hand will vibrate when the weapon utility is fully charged.  (similar to the left hand when magic is fully charged.)

- The gnomes are at it again.  The Bastard Sword now has its own utility function, as well.  "Pulse Wave" will knock back standard monsters that are in range, thus giving the adventurer a little breathing room.

Changes:

- (Bal Fix) Gladius attack cool down changed from 0.9 seconds to 1 second for better compatibility with new utility "Double Strike."

- (Bug Fix) Removed the obstacle component from the alter asset that was causing mobs to walk around it when they should be able to walk through it.

- (Bug Fix) Re-ordered the UI layers for the VR in-game HUD to avoid debuff icons rendering on top of the Game Over UI.

- (Bug Fix) Fixed bug that caused monsters to still be visible while the "Game Over" UI was enabled.

(v0.5.2)
Additions:
- The local Adventurer's Guild Research and Development department have discovered a magical network between dungeon alters.  Adventurers will now be able to teleport between previously activated alters to get around the dungeon slightly easier.

Changes:
- (Balance Fix) Stunning a monster with a full power melee attack or spell will now significantly decrease their attack cool down to further discourage weapon fanning strategies.  (It will be much more effective to hit+dodge+hit to give your weapon a chance to refresh and be able to stun the monster again).

- (QoL and Balance Fix) Duplicate weapons will now increase the weapon's base damage by 10%.  If a 10% increase does not reach a value of 1, the base damage will default to being increased by 1.  Duplicates with an enchantment will always apply the enchantment on to the currently equipped weapon, including replacing an existing enchantment.

- (Balance Fix) 'Monstrous Muscle' loot stat buff changed from 10% to 5%, and its text description has been updated to reflect the new percentage.

- (QoL and Balance Fix) Duplicate magic will now increase the spell's base damage by 10%.  If a 10% increase does not reach a value of 1, the base damage will default to being increased by 1.

notes.title: Things currently being worked on for Broken Dungeon v0.5.2
notes.content:
Good evening, Adventurers!

I just wanted to let everyone know some things I'm working on for Broken Dungeon.

Per player feedback, I will be adding a new method of locomotion to the game.  I have a working system in place that allows the adventurer to teleport from 1 activated alter to another.  This will let the adventurer return to parts of the dungeon they have previously visited.  It will not allow them to teleport to an alter they haven't activated yet, though.  So this feature would only come into effect if the adventurer has already unlocked 2 of the 3 alters on the floor.  Look forward to this being added to the beta for                 open testing soon.

Another change I am looking to make is how the player gains damage boosts.  At the moment, once you pick up your favorite weapon and spell, there is almost no need to open Weapon Racks or break Magic Crystals anymore.  To make these interactive objects more enticing, I am thinking of the following mechanic:
- Obtaining duplicate weapons or spells will add 10% damage to that specific weapon/spell.
- Swapping to a different weapon/spell will maintain the damage boost to that previous weapon/spell (i.e. if you got 3 dupes of the long sword so your long sword now deals 130% damage, and you swap to a battle axe, you can return to the long sword later, and it will still have the 130% damage boost)
- Picking up an enchanted weapon will count as a dupe and boost the weapon's stats, but you will also obtain the enchantment.  (i.e. if you have a gladius at 120% damage, and you pick up a Frost enchanted gladius, you will now have a Frost enchanted gladius at 130% damage)
- The Monsterous Muscle and Spirit Bottle loot will still apply their damage boosts to every weapon/spell type, but will only apply 1% per instead of the current 10%.  (This will make both the loot and duplicate weapon/spell beneficial to the adventurer).

Lastly, some player feedback suggested side-quests on the dungeon floor.  I like this idea.  Optional tasks that could be completed that would net the adventurer rewards at the risk of taking longer to complete the floor.

I am open to suggestions on what kind of side-quests the community would like to see.  Off the top of my head, I can think of things like challenge alters that will spawn a group of mobs that you must fight for a guaranteed reward, or puzzle alters that give you a chance to solve the puzzle for a guaranteed reward.  Perhaps, a skill based alter where you must toss a ball into a container from a short distance for a reward.

If you can think of other things you might like to see as optional tasks to make exploring a floor more interesting, please feel free to offer them up.

Thank you, again, to everyone that is offering up their opinions and critiques.  This is precisely what I was hoping for.

Keep on adventuring, everyone!!!
-Ken (SLAMS Games)

notes.title: Broken Dungeon v0.5.1 now in Beta status
notes.content:
Good evening, adventurers!!!

It has been 1 week since Early Access of Broken Dungeon launched.  I have already received some great input from some of you, and many of them are implemented in v0.5.1.  As some of these features cannot be truly tested by myself (i.e. Windows Mixed Reality support), the current version of 0.5.0.1 will remain the standard.  Players who wish to try out the latest changes simply need to opt into the Beta by right-clicking their game in Steam.  Then go to Properties > BETAS > v0.5.1_beta.

If I do not receive any messages regarding bugs, I will set v0.5.1 as the standard version of the game when the next Beta version is created.

Change log:
(v0.5.1)
Additions:
- It appears the local vampire coven have been a bit too busy.  On-hit blood effects can now be disabled in the options found in the Title scene.  (The weapon enchantment "Bleed" will still display dripping blood effects, as will monsters currently affected by it.)

- The local Adventurer's guild has received a request to re-engineer the first floor of the dungeon.  As such, hallway chunks #11, #12 and #13 have been added, and the 1st floor of the dungeon is now guaranteed to be much smaller and symmetrical to allow adventurers an easier time to buff up before truly diving into the depths.

Changes:
- (Misc) The options save file has been updated to accommodate the new "toggle blood" setting.

- (Misc) Tips cards 9 and 10 have been updated to accommodate new Windows Mixed Reality input support.

- (Bug Fix) Re-positioned torches in the large room within hallway chunk #9 to fix the issue of the center ceiling and floor not rendering light due to too many light sources.

- (Bug Fix) Removed 1 torch, and re-positioned the other within the Title scene to avoid the floor and ceiling not rendering lighting from the VR player's magic prior to the game starting due to too many light sources.

- (Misc) Procedural dungeon generation for floor 1 has been changed to use new dungeon chunks 11, 12 and 13 to force symmetrical dungeon designs.  Dungeon generation after floor 1 remains the same as it formerly was.

Other:
- Windows Mixed Reality support has been added.

==================================================================

As always, please feel free to offer your suggestions, critiques, and requests in the Steam forum for the game.  I plan to check it weekly at the very least to ensure I am answering questions and/or determining what I will need to work on for the next update.

I appreciate you all, and keep on adventuring!!!
-Ken (SLAMS Games)

notes.title: Broken Dungeon early access is now LIVE!!!!!!!!!
notes.content:
It's been a long time coming, but the day is finally here.

Broken Dungeon is now live as early access on Steam!!!

I thank everyone for their patience and support over the past couple of years leading me to this point.  I hope that you all enjoy Broken Dungeon and its future iterations as I continue to develop it.

As a reminder, please feel free to offer suggestions in the SLAMS community forum:
https://steamcommunity.com/groups/slamsgames

As a solo developer, I know that I only have a narrow view point on the game.  With everyone's help, I hope Broken Dungeon can evolve into the best possible game that it can be.

Thank you, everyone.
-Ken (SLAMS Games)

notes.title: Broken Dungeon v0.5.0 (Early Access Release Candidate)
notes.content:

Changes:
- (Bug Fix) Fixed logic discrepancy that caused the "Devil On Your Shoulder" to show multiple magic orbs at the same time.

- (Bug Fix) Corrected logic on melee weapon damage modifiers so the player doesn't lose 1 point of strength on every 3 Monstrous Muscle obtained.

- (Bug Fix) Further adjusted monster attack logic across all monsters for better damage timing results.

- (QOL Change) Changed the challenge goal to unlock the Vampiric Bite loot. The adventurer no longer needs to heal from below 10% to full in 1 map. The new challenge is to heal 10,000 points in total.

- (Bug Fix) Modified monster logic to stop the issue where if a monster was stun locked by player attacks, it would spin 180 degrees to re-navigate due to thinking it was stuck on terrain.

- (Balance Fix) Lowered Fire Bolt's damage from 20 to 15.

Other:
- Added debugging functionality to the procedural level generator class to allow forcing certain layouts to generate during development.

notes.title: Early Access Release - ETA April 20th, 2021
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!

I appreciate all of you who have taken a liking to Broken Dungeon and what it could become.  I am excited to announce that my current goal is to unlock Broken Dungeon's early access on April 20th, 2021.  Should everything go smoothly, I don't anticipate this date to change.

Additionally, free copies of the game will be offered to select streamers at the same time.

To maximize the exposure of Broken Dungeon to a wide audience range, streamers that will be considered for free copies must have at least 50,000 subscribers or followers to their Twitch, Youtube, or other streaming channels.  If you would like to apply for a free copy of Broken Dungeon, please shoot me an email at kenvernongames [at-symbol] gmail.com.  (Splitting up my email address here is just to mitigate bot spam).  Your email should include your name, and a link to your streaming channel.

Applications for a free copy of Broken Dungeon will be open until the end of April.  After which, I will no longer guarantee approval for requests that meet the requirements.  At that time, I will simply perform a case by case review as I have the time or a need arises.

Again, thank you very much for your support and the enthusiastic responses that I have heard from all of you taking a peak at Broken Dungeon.  I can't wait to see how Broken Dungeon evolves through the community's input and suggestions over the coming months.  Please help me make this the best game it can be.  ( :

-Ken (SLAMS Games)

notes.title: Beta test branch has been updated to v0.4.8
notes.content:
Broken Dungeon v0.4.8 Change Log:

======================================================

(Additions)
- Being secretive doesn't appear to be helpful, so the Broken Dungeon now shows the current version number at the title scene.

- Dungeon monsters can't seem to follow orders to remain sneaky.  Thus, adventurers now hear ominous laughter when the Dungeon Master skill is used.  Additionally, each Dungeon Master skill now has its own sound effect that is heard along with the laughter.

- The creator of Broken dungeon (essentially...me) has decreed that branding must be visible to prospective adventurers.  Thus, the SLAMS Games logo now plays at the start of the game.

- The Chimera's new shoes are lovely, but also noisy.  Chimeras now have walking sound effects.

======================================================

(Changes)
- The AI dungeon master has been advised that not every monster wants to group up in a party.  Thus, HARD difficulty has reduced cluster spawning from 100% chance to 75%.

- The AI dungeon master enjoys seeing its monsters born, so cluster spawning delays have increased to 2 seconds (up from 1.5 seconds) between monster spawns.

- The gods of the universe have deemed that too many visual resources are being used up by the Firestorm spell.  Thus, fewer cloud and rock particles will now be rendered to maintain quality.

- Just like with vegetables, a variety is better than always the same thing.  Thus, the AI Dungeon Master now has a 25% chance to purchase lower cost skills rather than always purchasing more expensive ones.

- Adventuring gnomes complained that aiming magic at an upward angle would cause controller oriented movement to reverse.  Thus, the controller orientation anchor has been adjusted to provide 30 additional degrees of upward aiming before forward movement reverses.  As a bonus effect, this has made underhand tossing of the Firestorm spell easier, as well.

- The local adventurer's guild has hired more literate employees.  Thus, the Tips and Tricks card #12 now more accurately describes soul gains from defeating floor bosses.

======================================================

(Other)
- As debuffs can be applied to both monsters and adventurers, adventurers went on strike over the prospect of the future Shock debuff stunning for 3 seconds.  Thus, the Shock debuff will cause a 50% reduction in damage dealt, instead.  (this debuff is still under development and I am simply noting the change in direction)

notes.title: Broken Dungeon v0.4.7 is now live!
notes.content:
Change log for Broken Dungeon v0.4.7:

- Sent monsters back to school to learn to stop dealing damage to the adventurer when they are affected by the frost debuff and still in their 'getting hit' animation.

- Ice Bolt and Frigid Javelin became best friends, and decided to trade clothes, including their former charge-up times.

- Arcane Bolt didn't go outside to play, and lost some muscle mass.  Arcane Bolt now deals less damage.

- Chain Lightning, on the other hand, went to the gym every day, and now deals more damage.

- Greedy little demons have begun raiding the dungeon, and taking all the legendary loot they can find.  
Thus, legendary tier loot now appears less often.

- The Broken Dungeon Olympics committee has deemed steroids for weapons are now illegal.  Thus, weapon damage across the board has been reduced for a more fair playing field.

- Bosses have learned to step more quietly due to complaints from their downstairs neighbors.  Bosses footstep sounds will now no longer penetrate as deeply into the dungeon.

- Monsters are now more interested in their fights with adventurers, and will look away less often during combat.

- Dying bosses have been scolded by the gods that they shouldn't still trigger AoE effects during their death animations.

- The local Adventurer's Guild has run out of funding, and can no longer provide the Firebolt spell to brand new adventurers.  Thus, adventurers now start with Arcane Bolt.

- Due to supply and demand, the cost of purchasing chests from the dungeon store has begun to fluctuate based on game difficulty.

- Bosses have grown a philanthropic conscience, and have decided to reward more souls based on the game difficulty.

- Credits given where credit is due.  A credits scene is now accessible from the title scene.

- Chests were sad that their opening animations were effectively ignored.  Thus, spawning loot from chests is now slightly delayed to better appreciate the chest's best trait.  Opening.

- VR Adventurer was formerly performing presidential secret service dives by blocking its own chain lightning spell.  The adventurer has been advised that they are not being paid to do this.

- The supervising Arch Magus has noticed that Chain Lightning was not spell-crafted correctly.  With the new corrections, Chain Lightning can now chain off of the adventurer if there isn't a nearer target in range to bounce to.  Additionally, monsters can now be chained to more than once if only it and another target are in range of each other.

- Discovered that dividing by zero creates paradoxical alternative realities.  Thus, the scoring logic has been adjusted to no longer show "0" scores due to invalid equations.

- Game Over means Game Over.  Adventurers can no longer kill monsters or bosses during the Game Over fade out.

- Dungeon Store got slammed with a demonic class action lawsuit for false advertising.  Now the point of sale orb displays the soul cost to purchase the chests.

notes.title: Broken Dungeon v0.4.6 Update
notes.content:
Leading up to the initial launch of Broken Dungeon's early access, here is a small update to fix a few bugs discovered during steam alpha testing, and a couple of quality-of-life changes:

- Fixed bug of tier 5 "boss" mobs staying in dungeon after adventurer goes to the store.
- Adjusted score calculation to better reward faster players.
- Added developer debugging functionality for VR view.
- Removed wait time to continue past early access disclaimer.
- Added hint to player to look behind them in Disclaimer scene.
- Increased DM mana regen per floor by 5% on easy difficulty.
- Changed fire enchant particles to inherit 15% of weapon's initial velocity to be slightly more dynamic.
- Increased chain lightning's chain distance from 6 to 10 meters.
